title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: example calendars dataset holds ready-made calendar objects. autoplot() (equivalent plot()) draws timeframe row rectangles sized timeslice’s share year:
code: data("calendars", package = "energyRt") names(calendars) #>  [1] "season_dn"                      "d365"                           #>  [3] "annual"                         "utopia_seasons"                 #>  [5] "unit_s4"                        "unit_s4h4"                      #>  [7] "d365_h24"                       "d365_h24_subset_1day_per_month" #>  [9] "m12"                            "m12a"                           #> [11] "q4"                             "s4"                             #> [13] "s4_h24"                         "m12_h24"                        #> [15] "wd7_h24"                        "w52_h24"                        #> [17] "s4_h24_subset_2seasons"         "m12_h24_subset_4months"         #> [19] "m12_subset_q1" autoplot(calendars$season_dn)

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: fill = "order" (default) color_pattern controls gradient. "within" (default) colours level timeslices — hourly row shows full h00→h23 cycle repeating every day, "global" colours absolute chronology across whole year.   fill metrics timeslice "share" "weight":
code: autoplot(calendars$d365_h24)                          # within (default) autoplot(calendars$d365_h24, color_pattern = "global") autoplot(calendars$season_dn, fill = "share")

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: cell can labelled individual level name ("name", default, e.g. h00…h23) full timeslice path ("timeslice", e.g. d001_h00). Label text auto-contrasts fill; override label_color.
code: # zoom (see below) so labels are legible autoplot(calendars$d365_h24,          show_leafs = list(YDAY = "d001", HOUR = 1:24),          label_by = "name")

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: show_leafs selects timeslices draw. Pass named list filter per timeframe level (character = timeslice names, numeric = positions among level’s timeslices), unnamed vector filter finest level directly.
code: # day 100, hours 5-10 autoplot(calendars$d365_h24, show_leafs = list(YDAY = "d100", HOUR = 5:10)) # the first 48 leaf timeslices (first two days) autoplot(calendars$d365_h24, show_leafs = 1:48)

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: reduced calendar can shown full reference calendar: pass full one reference. timeslices present subset filled; rest left empty.
code: autoplot(calendars$d365_h24_subset_1day_per_month,          reference = calendars$d365_h24)

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: border outlines rectangles (default dense rows read smooth gradient) palette picks viridis option; result ggplot can keep customizing :
code: autoplot(calendars$season_dn, palette = "magma", border = "grey40") +   labs(title = "Four seasons, day/night") +   theme_minimal()

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: autoplot() lays every timeslice one row per timeframe. value indexed two-dimensional calendar — day--year × hour, month × hour — heatmap reads naturally: plot_heatmap() puts finest timeframe y, next x, coarser levels facets. layout taken calendar (pass calendar =), guessed timeslice names tsl_guess_format(). synthetic hourly load profile d365_h24 calendar (daily cycle plus seasonal swing). diurnal band winter/summer contrast immediately visible:  Facet day--year format "month" get one day--month × hour panel per month:  palette selects viridis option name labels colour bar, exactly autoplot().
code: cal  <- calendars$d365_h24 tt   <- cal@timetable prof <- data.frame(   timeslice = tt$timeslice,   load  = 50 + 30 * sin(2 * pi * (tsl2hour(tt$timeslice) - 6) / 24) +                 15 * cos(2 * pi *  tsl2yday(tt$timeslice)      / 365))  plot_heatmap(prof, calendar = cal, value = "load")   # x = YDAY, y = HOUR plot_heatmap(prof, value = "load", facet = "month")  # 12 monthly panels

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: timeslice-indexed model data lays way. electricity demand solar capacity factor packaged UTOPIA kit, season × hour calendar (s4_h24): pull object getObject(), take one region (, demand, one year), pass timeslice + value columns plot_heatmap(). name argument carries value’s unit onto colour bar.   weather heatmap exactly autoplot() draws weather object directly — line area variants (see Weather ).
code: repo <- utopia_modules$electricity$R3$repo wcal <- calendars$s4_h24  DEM <- getObject(repo, name = "DEM_ELC", drop = TRUE) dem <- subset(as.data.frame(DEM@demand), region == "R1" & year == 2050) plot_heatmap(dem[, c("timeslice", "demand")], calendar = wcal, value = "demand",              name = "PJ") WSOL <- getObject(repo, name = "WSOL", drop = TRUE) wsol <- subset(as.data.frame(WSOL@weather), region == "R1") plot_heatmap(wsol[, c("timeslice", "wval")], calendar = wcal, value = "wval",              name = "capacity factor")

title: Plotting energyRt objects
text: commodity, autoplot() shows emission factors (@emis). Passing several commodities compares emission intensities side side.
code: COA <- newCommodity("COA", desc = "Coal",                     emis = data.frame(comm = "CO2", unit = "kt/GWh", emis = 0.33)) OIL <- newCommodity("OIL", emis = data.frame(comm = "CO2", unit = "kt/GWh", emis = 0.25)) GAS <- newCommodity("GAS", emis = data.frame(comm = "CO2", unit = "kt/GWh", emis = 0.18))  autoplot(COA)                 # a single commodity autoplot(COA, OIL, GAS)       # comparison

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: solver_options named list ready-made presets — one pins backend, solver, data-exchange format, solver-specific tuning: Use preset one two ways: set_default_solver() lasts session. make default stick across sessions, save en_config_write(); en_config_show() reports current default together solver paths depends . solve_model() interpolates model solves ; solve_scenario() solves already-interpolated scenario. solver = NULL scenario’s settings get_default_solver() used.
code: names(solver_options) solver_options$glpk solver_options$julia_highs_barrier # 1. Set it as the session default, then solve normally set_default_solver(solver_options$julia_highs) get_default_solver()                       # inspect the current default scen <- solve_model(model)                   # uses the default  # 2. Pass it explicitly to a single solve scen <- solve_model(model,  solver = solver_options$glpk) scen <- solve_scenario(scen,  solver = solver_options$gams_gdx_cplex)

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: GNU Linear Programming Kit. energyRt writes model GMPL/MathProg calls glpsol executable — lowest-friction option good default small medium models.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$glpk)

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: energyRt writes Pyomo ConcreteModel (data exchanged SQLite default, Arrow/feather *_arrow presets) solves configured solver. CBC open-source default; CPLEX GLPK also available.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$pyomo_cbc) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$pyomo_cplex_barrier)   # CPLEX barrier

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: energyRt writes JuMP model solves Julia. HiGHS (open-source) fast recommended choice large models; *_barrier, *_simplex *_parallel presets select HiGHS algorithm. Cbc, GLPK CPLEX also available.
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_highs)           # default (auto) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_highs_barrier)   # interior point solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$julia_highs_parallel)  # parallel simplex

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: GAMS license, energyRt can write run GAMS model. gams_gdx_* presets exchange data GDX (fast, native); gams_csv_* presets use text/CSV. *_barrier *_parallel presets inject tuned cplex.opt (LP method, threads, crossover, …).
code: solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$gams_gdx_cplex) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$gams_gdx_cplex_barrier)

title: Solver backends and solver_options
text: NEOS Server runs commercial solvers (CPLEX, …) free internet. model built locally solve dispatched NEOS, can use CPLEX without local license. Two families provided — via Pyomo (neos_pyomo_*) via GAMS (neos_gams_*, sent inlined text local GAMS install needed). NEOS requires email address, set via NEOS_EMAIL environment variable helper (one energyRt setting whose environment variable prefixed ENERGYRT_, Pyomo subprocess reads NEOS_EMAIL directly): low-level NEOS interface (submit/poll/fetch job, list solvers, …) also exported — see ?neos neos_* functions.
code: set_neos_email("you@example.org") solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$neos_gams_cplex) solve_model(model, solver = solver_options$neos_pyomo_cplex_barrier)

title: Introduction to energyRt
text: energyRt optimization model — around one hundred predefined equations, extendable newConstraint() — implemented four mathematical programming languages: GLPK / MathProg — open source; bundled Rtools Windows, works box; Julia / JuMP — open source, fast solvers like HiGHS; Python / Pyomo — open source, CBC/HiGHS others; GAMS — commercial standard energy-systems work. model object solves backend consistent results — start GLPK zero setup, switch faster institutional solver later without touching model. full mathematical formulation documented model equations PDF; solver backends article covers configuration.

text: Models assembled small set object types: technology converts inputs outputs chain input → use → activity → output; costs, capacity, availability, emissions secondary flows attach . model bricks article walks every object depth.

title: Introduction to energyRt
text: One fuel, one power plant, one demand — complete, solvable system:  Bind bricks space time, solve GLPK: Results come back tidy tables: model built 1.59 GW gas capacity — exactly enough deliver 50 PJ year — solution reports every flow, cost, capacity variable level detail.
code: GAS <- newCommodity("GAS", timeframe = "ANNUAL") ELC <- newCommodity("ELC", timeframe = "ANNUAL")  SUP_GAS <- newSupply("SUP_GAS", commodity = "GAS",                      supply = data.frame(cost = 6.0))   # fuel price, MEUR/PJ  EGAS <- newTechnology("EGAS",   input   = list(comm = "GAS"), output = list(comm = "ELC"),   ceff    = data.frame(comm = "GAS", cinp2use = 0.55),        # 55% efficient   invcost = list(invcost = 900),                              # MEUR/GW   fixom   = 25, cap2act = 31.536, olife = 25L)  DEM_ELC <- newDemand("DEM_ELC", commodity = "ELC",                      demand = data.frame(demand = 50))               # 50 PJ a year  draw(EGAS) mod <- newModel("HELLO",   data    = newRepository("parts", GAS, ELC, SUP_GAS, EGAS, DEM_ELC),   region  = "R1", discount = 0.05,   horizon = newHorizon(period = 2025:2040, intervals = c(1, 5, 10),                        mid_is_end = TRUE))  scen <- solve_scenario(interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE"),                        solver = solver_options$glpk,                        echo = FALSE)    # echo = FALSE silences the solver log getData(scen, "vObjective", merge = TRUE)   # total discounted system cost, MEUR #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   scenario name       value #>   <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> #> 1 BASE     vObjective 6677. getData(scen, "vTechCap",   merge = TRUE)   # capacity the model built, GW #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   scenario name     tech  region  year value #>   <chr>    <chr>    <chr> <chr>  <int> <dbl> #> 1 BASE     vTechCap EGAS  R1      2025  1.59 #> 2 BASE     vTechCap EGAS  R1      2030  1.59 #> 3 BASE     vTechCap EGAS  R1      2040  1.59

code: library(energyRt)  library(tidyverse) # for data manipulation and visualization my_solver <- get_default_solver() print(my_solver) set_default_solver(solver_options$julia_highs) get_scenarios_path() # define a commodity COM <- newCommodity("COM") # Declare a domestic supply (market) for the commodity SUP <- newSupply(   name = "SUP",    desc = "Domestic supply of commodity",   commodity = "COM",   availability = data.frame(     cost = 10 # costs or prices of the commodity     )   ) draw(SUP) DEM <- newDemand(   name = "DEM",   desc = "Final demand for commodity",   commodity = "COM",   dem = data.frame(     slice = "ANNUAL", # time-slices are defined in the calendar object     dem = 100     )   ) draw(DEM) # create a repository object to store the core model data world_repo <- newRepository(name = "world_repo", COM, SUP, DEM) # check content of the repository by type/class summary(world_repo) # check names of the repository objects names(world_repo) hello_calendar <- newCalendar() # default calendar with no sub-annual resolutions planning_2025 <- newHorizon(2025) planning_2025 planning_horizon <- newHorizon(   period = 2025:2050,    intervals = rep(5, 10)   ) planning_horizon mod <- newModel(   name = "MODEL",    region = "WORLD",   data = world_repo,   calendar = hello_calendar,   horizon = planning_2025,   discount = 0.05   ) class(mod) # solve for one year scen_2025 <- solve(mod, name = "HELLO_2025") summary(scen_2025) # solve for multi-year horizon by adding the horizon object scen_2050 <- solve(mod, name = "HELLO_WORLD",                     calendar = planning_horizon) summary(scen_2050)

code: source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/optimal2050/energyRt/master/inst/install.R") install_energyRt() install_energyRt(branch = "dev") install.packages("pak") pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/energyRt")  # or, with remotes: # install.packages("remotes") # remotes::install_github("optimal2050/energyRt") install.packages("pak")  # energyRt's direct CRAN imports (base packages are omitted): deps <- c(   "generics", "data.table", "DBI", "RSQLite", "tibble", "tidyr", "dplyr",   "rlang", "stringr", "lubridate", "purrr", "arrow", "progressr", "tictoc",   "cli", "zoo", "registry", "options", "glue", "plyr",   # suggested — plots and reports (optional but recommended, see section 7):   "ggplot2", "patchwork", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "tinytex", "sf" )  failed <- character(0) for (pkg in deps) {   ok <- tryCatch(     {       pak::pkg_install(pkg, ask = FALSE)       message("  [ok]   ", pkg)       TRUE     },     error = function(e) {       message("  [FAIL] ", pkg, ": ", conditionMessage(e))       FALSE     }   )   if (!ok) failed <- c(failed, pkg) }  if (length(failed) == 0) {   message("All dependencies installed — installing energyRt itself:")   pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/energyRt") } else {   message("Failed packages: ", paste(failed, collapse = ", ")) } pak::pkg_sysreqs("optimal2050/energyRt")   # lists the apt packages # e.g. sudo apt install libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev libxml2-dev

title: Model bricks
text: technology converts input commodities output commodities. Read diagram left--right four internal stages: cinp2use — much common use unit commodity input provides (e.g. converting fuels common energy basis). use2cact — use technology’s activity (central variable costs, availability capacity tied ). cact2cout — activity output commodity (efficiency / yield). three default 1.  four column headers box (inp, use, act, ) exactly stages; coefficient printed next flow scales.
code: input(s)  ──▶  use  ──▶  activity  ──▶  output(s)              cinp2use   use2cact      cact2cout BOILER <- newTechnology(   name = "BOILER", desc = "Gas boiler",   input  = data.frame(comm = "GAS",  unit = "PJ"),   output = data.frame(comm = "HEAT", unit = "PJ"),   ceff = data.frame(comm = c("GAS", "HEAT"),                     cinp2use  = c(1,  NA),                     cact2cout = c(NA, 0.9)),   # 90% efficiency   cap2act = 1) draw(BOILER)

title: Model bricks
text: several commodities interchangeable input (output) side, put group. group converted use (via ginp2use geff), member’s contribution bounded share (share.lo/share./share.fx). cinp2ginp converts commodity group’s common unit.  share range drawn square brackets next grouped commodity. Mixed units live coefficients. inputs outputs use different units conversion appear somewhere, use, activity cap2act agree — chain coefficient natural place . fuels PJ electricity GWh: ginp2use = 277.78 converts fuel group GWh (technology operates GWh), cap2act = 8760 matches (1 GW × 8760 h). work factor hand: convert("PJ", "GWh", 1) gives . See Units article unit declared convert() finds factor.
code: CHP <- newTechnology(   name = "CHP", desc = "Co-firing plant (coal + biomass)",   input = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO"), group = "fuel", unit = "PJ"),   output = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),   group = data.frame(group = "fuel", desc = "Blended fuel", unit = "PJ"),   # inputs are PJ but the output is GWh: the PJ->GWh conversion (1 PJ =   # 277.78 GWh) rides on `ginp2use`, so use/activity are measured in GWh   geff  = data.frame(group = "fuel", ginp2use = 277.78),   ceff  = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO", "ELC"),                     cinp2ginp = c(1, 1, NA),                     cact2cout = c(NA, NA, 0.4),     # 40% efficiency                     share.up  = c(1.0, 0.3, NA)),   # at most 30% biomass   cap2act = 8760)                                   # 1 GW x 8760 h = 8760 GWh draw(CHP)

title: Model bricks
text: Everything technology measured activity. Installed capacity limits maximum activity scalar cap2act: cap2act — “much product (activity, output commodity identical) produced per unit capacity”. units activity per capacity, number depends . power plant rated GW running flat year produces 8760 GWh, cap2act = 8760 activity GWh — cap2act = 31.536 plant activity PJ (1 GW × 8760 h = 31.536 PJ), convention UTOPIA uses. Capacity bounded capacity slot: stock (pre-existing), cap.lo//fx (total), ncap.lo//fx (new builds) ret.lo//fx (retirement). Availability factors af/afs bound activity within capacity: af.caps activity timeslice fraction capacity — maximum capacity factor per slice (PyPSA’s p_max_pu), af.lo must-run floor — afs bounds activity summed timeframe, afs timeslice = "ANNUAL" annual capacity-factor bound (e.g. afs.lo = 0.4 forces least 40% annual utilization). third variant, afc.* ceff slot, applies capacity-relative bound individual commodity flow instead total activity.

what: Capacity in input vs. output units
title: Model bricks
text: capacity tied activity, whether expressed input output units depends place efficiency. Keep cinp2use = 1 put loss output (cact2cout = 0.9) activity tracks input — capacity fuel-input units. Move efficiency input side instead capacity becomes output rating:  boilers 90% efficiency; differ unit capacity means (fuel input vs. heat output).
code: # capacity rated on OUTPUT (e.g. a 1 GW_e turbine): activity == output BOILER_out <- newTechnology(   name = "BOILER_out", desc = "Boiler rated by heat output",   input  = data.frame(comm = "GAS",  unit = "PJ"),   output = data.frame(comm = "HEAT", unit = "PJ"),   ceff = data.frame(comm = c("GAS", "HEAT"),                     cinp2use  = c(1 / 0.9, NA),   # efficiency on the input side                     cact2cout = c(NA, 1)),        # activity == heat output   cap2act = 1) draw(BOILER_out)

title: Model bricks
text: Auxiliary commodities extra flows tracked alongside main conversion — emissions (NOx, SO2, CH4, PM10, PM25), recovered HEAT, land, cooling WATER, construction MATerials, -products. declared aux linked aeff coefficient named <driver>2a<|inp>: driver scales flow: cinp (commodity input), cout (output), act (activity), cap (installed capacity), ncap (new capacity), storage terms; …2aout produces aux commodity (emissions, recovered heat, -products); …2ainp consumes (water, materials, energy). tab isolates one driver base technology (GAS → ELC).
code: aux_tech <- function(param, value, acomm = "AUX", unit = "unit") {   aeff <- data.frame(acomm = acomm, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)   aeff[[param]] <- value   newTechnology(     name = paste0("TECH_", param), desc = paste0("aux via ", param),     input  = data.frame(comm = "GAS", unit = "PJ"),     output = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),     ceff   = data.frame(comm = c("GAS", "ELC"), cinp2use = c(1, NA), cact2cout = c(NA, 0.4)),     aux    = data.frame(acomm = acomm, unit = unit),     aeff   = aeff) }

text: Real technologies carry several aux flows . coal plant might emit NOx, SO2, CH4, PM10 PM25, recover HEAT -product, consume cooling WATER construction MATerials — single aux/aeff pair, row filling driver column applies:
code: PLANT <- newTechnology(   name = "PLANT", desc = "Coal plant with a full aux inventory",   input  = data.frame(comm = "COA", unit = "PJ"),   output = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),   ceff = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "ELC"), cinp2use = c(1, NA), cact2cout = c(NA, 0.4)),   aux  = data.frame(     acomm = c("NOx", "SO2", "CH4", "PM10", "PM25", "HEAT", "WATER", "MAT"),     unit  = c("kt",  "kt",  "kt",  "kt",   "kt",   "PJ",   "Mm3",   "kt")),   aeff = data.frame(     acomm     = c("NOx", "SO2", "CH4",  "PM10", "PM25", "HEAT", "WATER", "MAT"),     act2aout  = c(0.20,  0.01,  0.001,  0.05,   0.03,   0.9,    NA,      NA),     act2ainp  = c(NA,    NA,    NA,     NA,     NA,     NA,     0.1,     NA),     ncap2ainp = c(NA,    NA,    NA,     NA,     NA,     NA,     NA,      2))) draw(PLANT)

title: Model bricks
text: Beyond physics baked process, can add linear constraints model variables. newConstraint() low-level form: name raw model variable, dimension (.), relation (eq) right-hand side (rhs). classic use economy-wide emission cap: newConstraintS() higher-level shortcut: instead naming variables pass semantic type ("capacity", "newcapacity", "inp", "", "share", "growth", …) subset processes, fills right variables — instance capping total new capacity technology:
code: CO2CAP <- newConstraint(   name = "CO2CAP", desc = "Economy-wide CO2 cap", eq = "<=",   for.each  = data.frame(year = c(2030, 2040, 2050), comm = "CO2"),   emissions = list(variable = "vEmsFuelTot"),         # LHS term   rhs       = data.frame(year = c(2030, 2050), rhs = c(5000, 2000)),   defVal    = Inf) CO2CAP@rhs        # the emission-cap path (interpolated over the horizon) #>   year  rhs #> 1 2030 5000 #> 2 2050 2000 # limit total new coal capacity across the horizon COALLIM <- newConstraintS(   name = "COALLIM", type = "newcapacity", eq = "<=",   for.sum = list(tech = "PLANT"), rhs = 50)

title: Scenario management: how models, scenarios, and solutions are organized
text: scenario one interpolated instance model: model compiled onto concrete calendar, horizon, region scope. Solving — possibly several times, several solvers — produces runs. disk: Three ideas notice: run owns artifacts. Solving scenario second backend overwrite anything: run keeps inputs, raw outputs, provenance, parsed solution. -memory scenario object holds ONE active solution time; switching read, re-solve. run’s location derived. Nothing stores “run X lives” — always <scenario>/runs/<run-id>/, computed demand. moved scenario folder strand runs. default: scenario.yml . names run bare read_solution(scen) resolves loading; save sets active run, may edit file point elsewhere. Let’s produce tree. run = "<label>" names run explicitly; without , label defaults solver directory name (e.g. "glpk"): scenario_run_info(scen, "glpk") returns one run’s full run.yml; read_solution(scen, run = "glpk") switches active solution; drop_scenario_run(scen, "glpk-alt") deletes run (active one force = TRUE). external working directory — outside scenario, run record — available via solve_scenario(solver.dir = "..."), transient = TRUE solves throwaway folder.
code: scenarios/<name_model_calendar_horizon>/ ├── scenario.yml        # manifest: model reference, calendar, horizon, │                       #   `default:` — the default run (edit it freely) ├── scen.RData          # the thin S4 shell (all big data lives beside it) ├── class · format · layout · logfile.csv ├── modInp/parameters/<param>/           # the (base) interpolated problem ├── problem.RData       # swap data for the base problem (see Variants) ├── model/…             # the model's data — only when embedded (see below) └── runs/               # one folder per solver run     ├── glpk/                            # a base-problem run     │   ├── run.yml     #   provenance: solver, cmdline, started/finished,     │   │               #   duration, status, objective, host, user     │   ├── solver/     #   the solver working dir; the solver writes its     │   │               #   own solver/output/ — never restructured     │   └── modOut/variables/<var>/      #   the parsed solution store     └── julia_highs/…                    # another backend, side by side scen <- interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE") |>   solve_scenario(solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE) scen <- solve_scenario(scen, solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE,                    force = TRUE, run = "glpk-alt") scenario_runs(scen)[, c("run", "status", "solver_name", "objective", "active")] #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   run      status solver_name objective active #>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>           <dbl> <lgl>  #> 1 glpk     solved glpk              300 FALSE  #> 2 glpk-alt solved glpk              300 TRUE scen <- save_scenario(scen, verbose = FALSE) #> Scenario 'BASE' saved in 'C:/Users/admin/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpyecMwD/sm-demo/scenarios/BASE_SM_smc' #> Directory size: 0.44 MB sort(list.files(scen@path)) #>  [1] "class"         "format"        "layout"        "logfile.csv"   #>  [5] "model"         "modInp"        "problem.RData" "runs"          #>  [9] "scen.RData"    "scenario.yml"

title: UTOPIA I: building the model

IMP_* objects add external supply price; EXP_* objects add external market buys price (capped, exports stay side business, objective): export price sits every technology’s levelized cost, model never builds capacity just export – sells genuine surplus. Two caps work together: exp.paces exports (annual 10 PJ spread timeslices via year-shares – bare exp.= 10 read 10 per timeslice), reserve bounds horizon total. Without pacing, model front-loads whole reserve base year, sunk fleet makes surplus cheapest.

title: UTOPIA I: building the model
text: Electricity demand follows deterministic load shape, weighted timeslice’s share year grown milestone years. Two views demand object: aggregated annual totals region (type = "area", default), within-year profiles region year (type = "line") – note morning ramp evening peak:
code: years  <- c(2020, 2030, 2040, 2050) growth <- c(1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6) annual_demand <- 100                                   # base-year PJ per region  share <- as.data.frame(cal@timeslice_share)[, c("timeslice", "share")] d0 <- merge(prof$demand, share, by = "timeslice") d0$w <- d0$load * d0$share dem_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(years), function(i) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(regions, function(r) {     dr <- d0[d0$region == r, ]     data.frame(region = r, year = years[i], timeslice = dr$timeslice,                demand = annual_demand * growth[i] * dr$w / sum(dr$w))   })) }))  DEM_ELC <- newDemand(   name = "DEM_ELC",   desc = "Final electricity demand",   commodity = "ELC",   unit = "PJ",   demand = dem_rows ) autoplot(DEM_ELC, years = 2020:2050) # autoplot(DEM_ELC, style = "line", years = c(2020, 2050)) # autoplot(DEM_ELC, style = "heatmap", years = c(2020, 2050))

title: UTOPIA I: building the model
text: Policies pathways pre-built objects layered onto base model running scenarios (mirroring IDEEA’s CO2_CAP etc.): CO2_CAP – declining cap CO2 emissions (newConstraint vEmsFuelTot; starts near BASE emissions (~5,000 kt/region 2020) tightens deep cut 2050); CT_CO2 – rising carbon tax (newTax; costs MEUR emissions kt, 20-80 EUR/t reads 0.02-0.08 MEUR/kt – watch units); RES_SHARE – growing renewable-generation floor; NO_NEW_NUC – new nuclear capacity; EARLY_RET – forced early retirement coal gas fleets (declining per-region ceiling installed coal gas capacity; optimizeRetirement = TRUE plants lets model choose units close).
code: nreg <- length(regions) CO2_CAP <- newConstraint(   name = "CO2_CAP",   eq = "<=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, comm = "CO2"),   term1 = list(variable = "vEmsFuelTot"),   rhs = data.frame(year = range(years), rhs = c(5000, 2500) * nreg),   defVal = Inf )  CT_CO2 <- newTax(   name = "CT_CO2",   comm = "CO2",   tax = data.frame(year = range(years), bal = c(0.02, 0.08))  # 20-80 EUR/t )  ren <- c("ESOL", "EWIN", "EHYD") sh  <- seq(0.15, 0.50, length.out = length(years)) RES_SHARE <- newConstraint(   name = "RES_SHARE",   eq = ">=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, comm = "ELC"),   term1 = list(variable = "vTechOut", for.sum = list(tech = ren)),   rhs = data.frame(year = years, rhs = sh * annual_demand * growth * nreg),   defVal = 0 )  NO_NEW_NUC <- newConstraint(   name = "NO_NEW_NUC",   eq = "<=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, tech = "ENUC"),   term1 = list(variable = "vTechNewCap"),   rhs = 0,   defVal = 0 )  # vTechCap is indexed by region, so this ceiling applies region by region. # for.each is the full year x tech grid (expand.grid, not a recycled # data.frame); rhs sets a declining per-region ceiling. The binding effect is # on GAS -- without it the model builds gas out as the flexible VRE backstop; # coal already phases out on economics. A full fossil exit is infeasible here # (must-run nuclear + limited transmission need firm capacity for peak), so the # schedule keeps a backup floor. defVal = Inf leaves 2020 unbound. EARLY_RET <- newConstraint(   name = "EARLY_RET",   eq = "<=",   # scope to 2030+ only: adding the 2020 milestone (even unbound) makes the LP   # infeasible through rhs interpolation.   for.each = expand.grid(year = c(2030, 2040, 2050), tech = c("ECOA", "EGAS"),                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE),   term1 = list(variable = "vTechCap"),   rhs = data.frame(     tech = rep(c("ECOA", "EGAS"), each = 3),     year = rep(c(2030, 2040, 2050), 2),     rhs  = c(12, 10, 8,   7, 6, 5)     # coal & gas ceilings (GW/region), falling   ),   defVal = Inf )

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: UTOPIA classic teaching model energy-system optimization: small Reference Energy System (RES) maps primary resources → conversion technologies → energy carrier → final demand, finds least-cost way meet demand planning horizon. vignette rebuilds UTOPIA energyRt end end – commodities, supply, demand, technologies (including renewables weather, storage, blended-fuel plant), multi-region layout, solves GLPK (bundled, external solver needed) analyses results. inputs deterministic shipped package: sub-annual calendars (calendars), representative capacity-factor / load profiles (utopia_weather, utopia_demand, utopia_stock), expanded regions [utopia_profiles()]. Time-resolution construction covered companion article; simply pick ready calendar. Units. Capacity GW, energy/activity PJ, costs MEUR, emissions kt. capacity--activity factor cap2act = 31.536 converts 1 GW running full year 31.536 PJ (1 GW x 8760 h). Cost figures illustrative, rounded values range published technology catalogues (e.g. Danish Energy Agency / NREL ATB): overnight capital cost EUR/kW (= MEUR/GW), fixed O&M EUR/kW/yr, fuel prices EUR/GJ (= MEUR/PJ).
code: library(energyRt) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) # keep all scenario files in a temporary folder set_scenarios_path(file.path(tempdir(), "utopia")) # capital-cost helper: EUR/kW -> MEUR/GW (numerically 1:1) meur_gw <- function(eur_per_kw) convert("EUR/kW", "MEUR/GW", eur_per_kw)

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: Electricity demand follows deterministic load shape utopia_demand (relative shape slice), scaled annual level per region grown horizon. utopia_profiles() already expanded shape regions.
code: share <- as.data.frame(cal@slice_share)[, c("slice", "share")] d0 <- merge(prof$demand, share, by = "slice") d0$w <- d0$load * d0$share                       # energy weight per slice years <- c(2020, 2030, 2040, 2050); growth <- c(1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6) dem_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(years), function(i) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(regs, function(r) {     dr <- d0[d0$region == r, ]     data.frame(region = r, year = years[i], slice = dr$slice,                dem = 100 * growth[i] * dr$w / sum(dr$w))   # ~100 PJ/yr in 2020   })) })) DEM <- newDemand("DEM_ELC", commodity = "ELC", dem = dem_rows)

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: Solar, wind hydro availability come representative capacity-factor profiles (utopia_weather, sourced reanalysis data). weather object holds capacity factor wval per region slice; technology references cap output.
code: wobj <- function(res) newWeather(res, timeframe = "HOUR",   weather = prof$weather[prof$weather$resource == res, c("region", "slice", "wval")]) WSOL <- wobj("WSOL"); WWIN <- wobj("WWIN"); WHYD <- wobj("WHYD")  # a quick look at the solar day-shape (summer vs winter) prof$weather |>   dplyr::filter(resource == "WSOL", region == "reg1",                 grepl("^(WIN|SUM)_", slice)) |>   dplyr::mutate(season = sub("_.*", "", slice),                 hour = as.integer(sub(".*_h", "", slice))) |>   ggplot(aes(hour, wval, colour = season)) + geom_line() +   labs(title = "Solar capacity factor by hour", y = "capacity factor") +   theme_bw()

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: Coal gas plants combust fuel (combustion = 1, CO2 counted) convert electricity given efficiency (ceff$cinp2use). Existing base-year capacity comes utopia_stock.
code: stk <- function(tech) {   g <- prof$stock[prof$stock$tech == tech, ]   data.frame(region = g$region, year = 2020, stock = g$gw) } thermal <- function(nm, comm, eff, inv, fixom) newTechnology(nm,   input = list(comm = comm, combustion = 1), output = list(comm = "ELC"),   ceff = data.frame(comm = comm, cinp2use = eff), cap2act = 31.536, fixom = fixom,   invcost = data.frame(region = regs, invcost = inv),   olife = 30L, start = 2010L, capacity = stk(nm), optimizeRetirement = TRUE)  ECOA <- thermal("ECOA", "COA", 0.40, meur_gw(2000), 55)   # coal EGAS <- thermal("EGAS", "GAS", 0.58, meur_gw(900), 25)    # CCGT ENUC <- newTechnology("ENUC", input = list(comm = "NUC"), output = list(comm = "ELC"),   ceff = data.frame(comm = "NUC", cinp2use = 0.35), af = data.frame(af.lo = 0.7),   cap2act = 31.536, fixom = 120, invcost = data.frame(region = regs, invcost = meur_gw(6500)),   olife = 50L, start = 2010L, capacity = stk("ENUC"))

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: ECOABIO coal-biomass co-firing plant: burns blend two fuels. fuels sit one input group FUEL; group converts electricity (geff$ginp2use), fuel contributes group total (ceff$cinp2ginp), biomass share bounded (ceff$share.– 30% ). commodity-group / share machinery nutshell. feasible blend band requires solve – tech_share_frontier() intersects fuel’s share bounds: levelized cost look blend plant isolation. levcost() builds solves tiny single-technology model; using annual commodities makes LCOE read directly MEUR per PJ.
code: ECOABIO <- newTechnology("ECOABIO", desc = "Coal-biomass co-firing (blended fuel)",   input  = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO"), group = "FUEL", combustion = c(1, 0)),   output = list(comm = "ELC"),   group  = data.frame(group = "FUEL", desc = "Blended solid fuel", unit = "PJ"),   geff   = data.frame(group = "FUEL", ginp2use = 0.40),   ceff   = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO"), cinp2ginp = c(1, 1),                       share.up = c(1.0, 0.30)),   cap2act = 31.536, fixom = 60, invcost = data.frame(region = regs, invcost = meur_gw(2200)),   olife = 30L, start = 2010L, optimizeRetirement = TRUE) tech_share_frontier(ECOABIO)          # feasible coal/biomass share band ELCa <- newCommodity("ELCa", timeframe = "ANNUAL") ECOABIO_lc <- newTechnology("ECOABIO", desc = "Coal-biomass co-firing",   input  = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO"), group = "FUEL", combustion = c(1, 0)),   output = list(comm = "ELCa"),   group  = data.frame(group = "FUEL", desc = "Blended solid fuel", unit = "PJ"),   geff   = data.frame(group = "FUEL", ginp2use = 0.40),   ceff   = data.frame(comm = c("COA", "BIO"), cinp2ginp = c(1, 1), share.up = c(1.0, 0.30)),   cap2act = 31.536, fixom = 60, invcost = list(invcost = meur_gw(2200)), olife = 30L) lc <- levcost(ECOABIO_lc, discount = 0.05, verbose = FALSE,   repo = newRepository("r", COA, BIO, CO2, ELCa), fuel_costs = c(COA = 2.5, BIO = 8.0)) lc$levcost_npv                        # NPV levelized cost, MEUR/PJ autoplot(lc, type = "components")     # cost breakdown by year # a full technology datasheet (schematic, tables, share frontier, LCOE): report(ECOABIO_lc, format = "html", discount = 0.05,        repo = newRepository("r", COA, BIO, CO2, ELCa))

what: Assemble and solve the base scenario
title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: Interpolate model milestone years, solve scenario GLPK. Building scenario two steps – interpolate_model() solve_scenario() – pattern reuse every scenario .
code: repo <- newRepository("utopia",   COA, GAS, BIO, NUC, SOL, WIN, HYD, ELC, CO2,   SCOA, SGAS, SBIO, SNUC, SSOL, SWIN, SHYD, WSOL, WWIN, WHYD,   ECOA, EGAS, ENUC, ESOL, EWIN, EHYD, ECOABIO, STG, DEM) mod <- newModel("UTOPIA", data = repo, calendar = cal, region = regs,                 horizon = hor, discount = 0.05) scen_BASE <- solve_scenario(   interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE"), solver = solver_options$glpk) getData(scen_BASE, "vObjective", merge = TRUE)$value   # total system cost, MEUR

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: declining cap total CO2 emissions, tightening 40% base level:
code: base_emis <- getData(scen_BASE, "vEmsFuelTot", comm = "CO2", merge = TRUE) |>   group_by(year) |> summarise(v = sum(value), .groups = "drop") cap0 <- base_emis$v[base_emis$year == 2020] CO2CAP <- newConstraint(name = "CO2CAP", eq = "<=",   for.each = data.frame(year = years, comm = "CO2"),   term1 = list(variable = "vEmsFuelTot"),   rhs = data.frame(year = c(2020, 2050), rhs = round(cap0) * c(1.0, 0.4)),   defVal = Inf) scen_CO2CAP <- solve_scenario(   interpolate_model(mod, name = "CO2CAP", CO2CAP), solver = solver_options$glpk)

title: UTOPIA: a teaching energy-system model with energyRt
text: rising tax CO2 emissions: Compare emissions across scenarios:
code: CTAX <- newTax(name = "CTAX", comm = "CO2",   tax = data.frame(year = c(2020, 2050), bal = c(20, 80))) scen_CTAX <- solve_scenario(   interpolate_model(mod, name = "CARBONTAX", CTAX), solver = solver_options$glpk) lapply(list(BASE = scen_BASE, CO2CAP = scen_CO2CAP, CTAX = scen_CTAX),   function(s) getData(s, "vEmsFuelTot", comm = "CO2", merge = TRUE)) |>   bind_rows() |>   group_by(scenario, year) |> summarise(ktCO2 = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>   ggplot(aes(factor(year), ktCO2, fill = scenario)) +   geom_col(position = "dodge") + labs(x = "year", title = "CO2 emissions by scenario") +   theme_bw()

title: Energy Systems Modeling Toolbox
text: complete model — one fuel, one power plant, one demand — built, solved read ~20 lines (GLPK, external setup needed Windows Rtools): Get started vignette walks example ideas behind .
code: library(energyRt)  GAS <- newCommodity("GAS", timeframe = "ANNUAL") ELC <- newCommodity("ELC", timeframe = "ANNUAL")  SUP_GAS <- newSupply("SUP_GAS", commodity = "GAS",                      availability = data.frame(cost = 6.0))   # fuel price, MEUR/PJ  EGAS <- newTechnology("EGAS",   input   = list(comm = "GAS"), output = list(comm = "ELC"),   ceff    = data.frame(comm = "GAS", cinp2use = 0.55),        # 55% efficient   invcost = list(invcost = 900),                              # MEUR/GW   fixom   = 25, cap2act = 31.536, olife = 25L)  DEM_ELC <- newDemand("DEM_ELC", commodity = "ELC",                      dem = data.frame(dem = 50))               # 50 PJ a year  mod <- newModel("HELLO",   data    = newRepository("parts", GAS, ELC, SUP_GAS, EGAS, DEM_ELC),   region  = "R1", discount = 0.05,   horizon = newHorizon(period = 2025:2040, intervals = c(1, 5, 10),                        mid_is_end = TRUE))  scen <- solve_scenario(interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE"),                        solver = solver_options$glpk)  getData(scen, "vObjective", merge = TRUE)   # total discounted system cost getData(scen, "vTechCap",   merge = TRUE)   # capacity the model built, GW

Returning data native resolution unless asked otherwise safer default: old one silently summed 8760-slice hourly series single annual number, reads plausible value rather error, indistinguishable genuine annual result. Aggregation easy ask hard notice wanted. Code relied annual totals must now pass timeframe = "lowest" explicitly. geoframe controls spatial aggregation results carry region column, spatial twin timeframe. One "finest" (default, native resolution stored), "coarsest" (aggregate top geoscale level), "" (return every level stacked), explicit geoscale level name (e.g. "zone", "nation"). Requires geoscale model; without one inert. Inter-regional flow variables (e.g. vTradeIr) returned unchanged, summing flow across regions double-counts — spatial counterpart leaving state variables alone timeframe. process TRUE, dimensions "tech", "stg", "trade", "imp", "expp", "dem", "sup" renamed "process". parameters TRUE, parameters included search returned found. variables TRUE, variables included search returned found. maps TRUE, map-type parameters (membership mappings, value column) also returned. ignore.case grepl parameter regular expressions used '...' 'name_'. newNames renaming sets, named character vector list new names values, old names names - input parameter renameSets function. operation performed merging data (merge parameter). newValues revalue sets, named character vector list new values values, old values names - input parameter revalueSets function. operation performed merging data (merge parameter). na.rm TRUE, NA values dropped. digits integer, indicates number decimal places rounding, NULL - actions. drop.zeros logical, rows containing zero values filtered . asTibble logical, data.frames converted tibbles. stringsAsFactors logical, sets values converted factors? yearsAsFactors logical, year converted factors? Set 'year' integer default. scenNameInList logical, name scenarios used provided list several scenarios? variants logical, default TRUE: attach technology-variant provenance columns base, vintage cluster (scenario@modInp@sets$tech_variant) returned data, results vintaged / clustered technology can grouped rolled dimensions without parsing variant names. effect model variants, returned shape unchanged models. Set FALSE suppress columns. verbose logical, print progress diagnostic messages. interpolate TRUE, expand year-bearing object slots target years using parameter's default interpolation rule (quick demonstration plots). text: Collects building blocks "mix" chart solved scenario one tidy data.frame: technology output, storage charge/discharge, inter-regional rest--world trade, demand. extractor feeds autoplot(scenario, ...), scenario report, custom analysis (including sonification – see useR! training course).

code: getMix(   scen,   type = c("generation", "capacity", "new_capacity", "fuel"),   comm = "ELC",   region = NULL,   year = NULL,   timeslice = NULL,   drop_small = 0,   by = NULL,   top_n = NULL )

title: Extract a tidy mix (generation, capacity, fuel) from a solved scenario — getMix
text: scen solved scenario object, named list scenarios (results row-bound list names scenario column). type character: "generation" (default – output comm process, storage-exports negative), "capacity" (vTechCap + vStorageOutCap), "new_capacity" (vTechNewCap + vStorageOutNewCap), "fuel" (technology fuel consumption vTechInp input commodity). comm character, balanced commodity "generation" (default "ELC"). Ignored types. region character vector NULL (regions). Inter-regional trade flows meaningful region subset skipped region = NULL (cancel -region sum). year integer vector NULL (milestone year). timeslice NULL annual sums, regular expression selecting timeslice sample (e.g. "^SUM_" summer day s4_h24 calendar). matched timeslices carry hour tag ("_h00"..."_h23"), integer hour column added. drop_small numeric [0, 1): drop processes whose total absolute value share largest process (default 0, keep ). Unlike top_n DELETES rows – stacked charts lose mass. character vector, "vintage" "cluster". Technology variants always rolled back base technology process; default (NULL) simply summed, charts fragment one series per variant. Naming dimension keeps extra grouping column ("(none)" processes variants), ready drive fill facet. top_n integer: keep top_n largest processes (summed absolute value) lump rest one "" series. Mass-preserving – lumped rows re-aggregated, dropped – demand overlay never lumped. NULL (default) Inf keeps every process. Applied drop_small. list scenarios lumping runs per scenario, keeps top set.

title: Extract a tidy mix (generation, capacity, fuel) from a solved scenario — getMix
text: tidy data.frame columns scenario, type, process, flow (generation, storage-/, import/export, demand, fuel, capacity, new_capacity), comm, region, year, value, – timeslice given – timeslice (+ hour parsable), plus column named . text: object object class calendar. ... Passed plot_calendar(). fill One "order" (chronology, default), "share" (year-share timeslice), "weight" — metric mapped rectangle fill color. color_pattern fill = "order", color gradient applied: "within" (default) colors level timeslices — full h00→h23 gradient recycled every day, d001→d365 year — row shows cyclical structure; "global" colors absolute chronology (leaf order 1…n, e.g. 0…8760). Ignored "share"/"weight". palette Viridis color option (e.g. "D", "C", "magma") fill scale. labels Logical; draw labels inside rectangles (master /). label_by label rectangle : "name" (default) individual level name (e.g. HOUR cells become h00…h23, YDAY cells d001…d365), "timeslice" full timeslice path (e.g. d001_h00), "none". label_color Text color labels. "auto" (default) contrasts label cell — white darker part gradient, dark lighter part — labels stay readable dark fills. Pass single color (e.g. "black", "white") use labels. max_labels Integer; timeframes timeslices left unlabeled avoid clutter. border Rectangle outline color. NA (default) draws outline, high-resolution row (e.g. 8760 hourly timeslices) reads smooth gradient instead solid block borders. Pass e.g. "grey30" outline timeslices coarse calendars. show_leafs Select timeslices draw (NULL, default, shows ). Colors stay stable (e.g. h05 keeps color whether hours shown). reference Optional full calendar. supplied, x treated subset reference: plot lays reference's full structure fills timeslices present x (matched timeslice name), leaving unselected timeslices empty. Re-render even existing files date. title: Report template helpers — report_helpers
text: report_output(): Detect current render target: "html", "word", "latex". Outside knitr/pandoc context default returned. report_setup(): Setup-chunk boilerplate: chunk options (echo/warning/message ) per-output knitr.kable.NA placeholder. Returns detected output invisibly, templates can open fmt <- energyRt::report_setup(). report_layout(): one sizing system: named fractions text width shared outputs, plus raster dpi. report_esc(): Escape string current output (TeX escaping "latex", HTML escaping otherwise – Word content goes pandoc markdown, HTML entities safe). report_fmt_val(): Fixed-notation value formatting – never scientific ("1.2e+03"); "--" missing. report_img(): Emit image fraction line width; way images enter report page. report_img_row(): Emit ROW images (logos, banners, badges) spanning frac_total line width, split evenly gap . Missing files dropped silently; single image capped half frac_total lone logo span page. report_pagebreak(): Emit page break: always-break <div> HTML (honoured printing), \newpage LaTeX, raw {=openxml} block Word. Call results='asis' chunk. report_plot_png(): Rasterise ggplot dpi return png path (uniform pipeline three formats; avoids knitr fig options, docx partly rejects). report_sec(): Section divider + bold title (+ gray note); Word gets markdown heading. report_tbl(): One table pipeline: prune empty columns, round numerics, kable per format. kable escaping (single-escaped, never double). Large tables stay readable: HTML table 15 rows renders inside scrollable box sticky header (scroll = FALSE disables); max_rows caps printed rows "... K rows (N)" footer – PDF/Word additionally enforce 200-row safety cap max_rows given. report_css(): Emit shared report stylesheet (HTML ; -op Word LaTeX). report_header(): Page header: name + description left, optional image (logo) right.

all other regions     fixom = c(100, 200, 150) # MW a year   ),   varom = data.frame( # variable operational and maintenance cost     region = c("R1", "R2"), # regions     varom = c(1, 2) # $1 and $2 per MWh   ),   invcost = data.frame( # investment cost     year = c(2020, 2030, 2040), # to differentiate by years     invcost = c(1000, 900, 800) # $1000, $900, $800 per MW   ),   vintage = data.frame( # investment window and operational life     start = 2020, # can be installed from 2020     end = 2040, # can be installed until 2040     olife = 30 # operational life, years   ),   capacity = data.frame( # existing capacity     year = c(2020, 2030, 2040), # to differentiate by years     region = c("R1"), # exists only in R1     stock = c(300, 200, 100) # age-based exogenous retirement   ),   # regions where the technology can be installed   region = c("R1", "R2", "R5", "R7"), ) draw(ECOAL)

title: Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic) — utopia_profile
code: utopia_profile(   shape = c("step", "sine", "cosine", "hex"),   levels = 4L,   calendar = "s4_h24",   regions = NULL,   vary = c("none", "phase", "amplitude"),   min = 0,   max = 1,   period = c("year", "frame"),   phase = 0 )

title: Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic) — utopia_profile
text: shape "step" (ascending staircase levels plateaus: 0, 1/(levels-1), ..., 1), "sine", "cosine", "hex" (trapezoid ramp/plateau/ramp equal thirds). levels integer >= 2, number plateaus shape = "step" (ignored otherwise). levels = 2 /case. calendar calendar object, name shipped calendar (see calendars), timetable data.frame. regions optional character vector. NULL returns bare shape (timeslice, step, value); otherwise shape replicated per region leading region column. vary per-region variation (needs regions): "none" replicates identically; "phase" shifts region (-1)/n period (gradient across map – neighbouring regions peak sequence); "amplitude" scales region 's amplitude 1 - (-1)/(2(n-1)) (1 1/2 – good sites poor sites). min, max numeric range unit shape scaled (value = min + shape * (max - min)). period "year" (one cycle calendar) "frame" (one cycle inside parent timeframe finest level). phase numeric, fraction period shape shifted (applied regions, top vary = "phase" offsets).

title: Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic) — utopia_profile
text: tidy data.frame, chronologically ordered: region (regions given), timeslice (calendar's finest level), step (integer plateau index 0..levels-1 "step", NA otherwise – pretty-number handle hand-checkable inputs), value [min, max].

title: Synthetic input shapes on a calendar (deterministic) — utopia_profile
text: shape spans period : "year" stretches whole calendar; "frame" repeats inside parent timeframe (e.g. season's hours get diurnal shape). Slice positions midpoints timeslice's share along calendar's chronological chain, unequal slices land belong; cycle's anchor alphabetically first timeslice (rotate phase).
